history.dynasty: Kullu princely state (Raja Jagat Singh, mid-17th century)
history.summary: The Raghunath temple at Manikaran was the ORIGINAL home of the Rama (Raghunath) murti that Raja Jagat Singh of Kullu brought from Ayodhya in the mid-17th century as an act of atonement. Since the mid-1600s the murti has been installed in the Raghunath temple at Kullu town (a separate site - not a duplicate), while the Manikaran temple remains functional, maintained by a trust and offering a free langar to visitors. Pilgrims cook rice and dal in the nearby hot springs. Coordinates are town-level geocode (verify for exact temple location). Festival schedule and opening hours UNVERIFIED (verify).

name: Raghunath (Rama) Temple, Manikaran
town_description: Manikaran is a pilgrimage town in the Parvati Valley of Kullu district, at about 1,760 m on the banks of the Parvati river. Its hot sulphur springs are sacred to both Hindus (legend of Shiva and Parvati's lost earring) and Sikhs (Guru Nanak's visit), drawing pilgrims year-round. The town lies ~45 km from Kullu and ~3 km from Kasol, and is a trailhead for treks such as Kheerganga.
